newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin says import surcharge to boost CPI.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin says import surcharge to boost CPI.

text.p: Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said on Friday he expected a planned import surcharge to increase annual inflation by two to three percentage points later this year.
Kozlik also said that a planned increase in some state- regulated prices would increase the annual inflation rate by another percentage point.

"We expect the surcharge to have (a) negative effect on consumer prices, and we forecast it to push the annual CPI (consumer price index) up by some two to three percentage points," Kozlik told a news conference.
Slovakia, facing serious foreign trade problems, will add a 7.0 percent import surcharge on all goods except raw materials, effective July 21.
The surcharge will be cut to 5.0 percent of the declared value of the imported goods at the beginning of next year and to 3.0 percent from July 1998. It should be abolished on January 1, 1999.
Bratislava has had one of the lowest inflation rates among Europe's post-communist countries over the past two years. June consumer prices rose 0.3 percent after a 0.1-percent increase in May.
Annual inflation in June was 6.2 percent, compared with May's 6.1 percent increase.
"The increase in regulated prices will not be a significant move, but it is still forecast to add around one percentage point to annual inflation," Kozlik said.
The most significant jump in regulated prices will be a 10-percent rise in energy prices for corporate customers and a 10-percent hike in heating prices for citizens, effective from August.
Kozlik said the import surcharge should not hurt Slovakia's chances for integration into the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OCED).
But he would not comment on whether the government still expected to win OECD membership by year end, as planned.
Kozlik said the surcharge should affect some 70 to 80 percent of all Slovakia's imports and bring some 10 billion crowns ($289.8 million) a year to the state budget.
-- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402 ($ = 34.50 Slovak Crowns)
